tally.citation: Epic Goal 2 requires both engines to emit the same blocking/non-blocking verdict contract, and the ADR 0123 deliverable must record the engine design; the agentic branch in _run_plan_review skips the drift floor and xcheck steps that rewrite verdict and blocking, so the agentic verdict is not the same contract.
tally.title: Agentic verdicts skip drift floor and cross-checks

tally.citation: Epic's agentic engine deliverable (agentic_verdict.py adapt_findings, agentic.py, plan-review.yaml agentic_review step) builds a PASS from findings alone with no tool-call check; the epic's fail-closed invariant and AC on INDETERMINATE for incomplete runs are the claimed behavior this bug says is violated.
tally.title: Agentic plan review signs a PASS with zero tool calls

tally.citation: Acceptance criterion 'provider-parity and prompt evals pass on the new models' and child ticket 'Move prompt-eval spec model pins to the 5.5 ids and record before/after prompt evals' claim passing evals, but this bug reports seven plan-review criterion specs failing schema validation on the 5.5 run.
tally.title: Prompt evals: plan-review criterion specs fail with "'dimension' is a required property" schema error

tally.citation: Same eval subsystem as the AC 'provider-parity and prompt evals pass on the new models' and the child 'Move prompt-eval spec model pins to the 5.5 ids', but the missing solver in eval_solver.py:423 for plan-review-container/finder/isf-finder is a pre-existing gap the epic never claimed to add or change.
tally.title: Live prompt-eval loop has no solver for plan-review-container, -finder and -isf-finder specs (coverage 0.00)

tally.citation: The defect is in the pre-existing provider_parity harness tracker resolution (gate_source.gate_read_root, provider_parity.py:355), which the epic only consumes to run its provider-parity AC; the epic never changed or claimed fresh-worktree tracker attachment.
tally.title: provider_parity harness fails in a fresh worktree until a CLI call attaches .tickets-tracker

tally.citation: The bug is in the Bedrock spend-cap Lambda and its ceiling table (infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap), which the epic never changed or claimed; it is adjacent to the epic's child 'Point deploy model defaults and Bedrock alarms at the 5.5 inference profiles', but the epic's ACs cover only rebar.toml, bedrock.toml, MODEL_WINDOW_LADDER and the plan-review engine.
tally.title: Bedrock spend-cap metered estimate ran about 3x settled billing on 2026-11-12, above the README's documented band

tally.citation: Mismatch: the bug concerns release-tag type in docs/releasing.md and the release.yml github_release job, while the epic covers the plan-review engine switch, the agentic review engine, the 5.5 model upgrade, and ADR 0123; no AC or child ticket touches release tagging.
tally.title: docs/releasing.md says release tags are annotated, but release.yml creates lightweight tags (v0.13.1, v0.14.0, v0.15.0)
